question.text: Which organism eats only meat?

results.hint: Domestic cats are obligate members of this dietary group.
results.explanation: Carnivores get their food from animals; herbivores eat plants, while omnivores eat both.

question.text: What is the term for a person from Bulgaria?

results.hint: The standard demonym uses the country's name with the common -ian ending.
results.explanation: Bulgarian is also the name of Bulgaria's official language.

question.text: Which famous Russian ruler gave a Faberge egg as a gift to his wife, Alexandra?

results.hint: He was the final emperor of Russia, deposed during the 1917 revolution.
results.explanation: Nicholas II continued the Romanov tradition of commissioning jeweled Easter eggs from Fabergé, often with a hidden surprise inside.

question.text: Which author wrote 'Hamlet'?

results.hint: The same English playwright wrote Macbeth and Romeo and Juliet.
results.explanation: Hamlet is one of Shakespeare’s tragedies, alongside Macbeth and King Lear.

question.text: In which iconic '90s film did Leonardo DiCaprio play the role of Jack Dawson?

results.hint: The story centers on a doomed ocean liner that strikes an iceberg during its maiden voyage.
results.explanation: Titanic won 11 Academy Awards, tying the record then held by Ben-Hur.

question.text: With which sport is Michael Jordan associated?

results.hint: He became a global sports star while playing for the Chicago Bulls.
results.explanation: Basketball star Michael Jordan led the Chicago Bulls to six NBA titles and was named Finals MVP each time.

question.text: What word is used in the NATO Phonetic Alphabet for the letter B?

results.hint: In the radio spelling sequence, it comes between the code words for A and C.
results.explanation: Bravo is the NATO code word for B. The alphabet uses distinct words to make letters easier to understand over noisy radio links.

question.text: What type of alcoholic beverage is bourbon?

results.hint: Its mash must contain at least 51% corn, and it is aged in new charred oak barrels.
results.explanation: Bourbon is a style of American whiskey made from a grain mash containing at least 51% corn.

question.text: Where would you find the city of Brussels?

results.hint: The country lies in western Europe, between France, Germany, and the Netherlands.
results.explanation: Belgium is part of the Benelux region with the Netherlands and Luxembourg. Brussels also hosts major institutions of the European Union.

question.text: Which influential historical person was an industrialist who revolutionised mass-production techniques?

results.hint: A moving assembly line helped him make the Model T affordable to ordinary buyers.
results.explanation: Henry Ford's company made the Model T, and assembly-line production helped make cars affordable to many Americans.

What animal is known as Orcinus orca?

results.hint: This black-and-white marine mammal is the largest member of the oceanic dolphin family.
results.explanation: Killer whale is the common name for Orcinus orca. Despite the name, it is the largest dolphin species.

question.text: Which bird often stands on one leg?

results.hint: Its large pink flocks are famous for wading through shallow water.
results.explanation: Flamingos filter tiny organisms from water and mud with their distinctive bills, which they hold upside down while feeding.

question.text: The 100-meter butterfly and 100-meter freestyle are both events in what Olympic sport?

results.hint: These races take place in a pool, with butterfly and freestyle naming two techniques.
results.explanation: Swimming includes four competitive strokes: butterfly, freestyle, backstroke and breaststroke.

question.text: What is the unit of linear measurement?

results.hint: Centimeters and kilometers are both scaled subdivisions or multiples of this standard length unit.
results.explanation: The meter is defined using the speed of light in a vacuum: light travels one meter in 1/299,792,458 of a second.

question.text: Where in the world would you most expect to be served Haggis?

results.hint: It is traditionally served at Burns Night suppers honoring poet Robert Burns.
results.explanation: Scotland's Burns suppers often feature haggis, famously celebrated in Robert Burns's poem “Address to a Haggis.”

question.text: With which sport is Rafael Nadal associated?

results.hint: His dominance at the French Open earned him the nickname “King of Clay.”
results.explanation: Tennis star Rafael Nadal earned the nickname “King of Clay” for his success on clay courts, especially at the French Open.

question.text: With which sport is Manny Pacquiao associated?

results.hint: He is an eight-division world champion who competed in a roped ring.
results.explanation: Boxing made Manny Pacquiao an international star, and he won world titles in eight different weight divisions.

question.text: For what does the fourth letter in "NASA" stand?

results.hint: The first three words of NASA’s full name are National Aeronautics and Space.
results.explanation: The fourth letter stands for Administration, completing National Aeronautics and Space Administration. NASA was established in 1958 to lead the U.S. civilian space program.

question.text: In Greek mythology, Carina represents the keel, Puppis represents the stern, and Vela represents the sails of which mythological ship captained by Jason?

results.hint: Jason's crew sought the Golden Fleece aboard it.
results.explanation: The Argo was named for its builder, Argus, and carried Jason's crew on their quest for the Golden Fleece.

question.text: Which piece of written work starts with the line 'Lolita, light of my life, fire of my loins.'?

results.hint: Its author was a Russian-American novelist celebrated for intricate prose and wordplay.
results.explanation: Lolita is narrated by Humbert Humbert, whose elaborate voice is established from the opening line.

question.text: Which song begins with the lyrics: "When I find myself in times of trouble, Mother Mary comes to me / Speaking words of wisdom, let it be..."?

results.hint: Its title repeats the final phrase in the lyrics quoted in the question.
results.explanation: “Let It Be” was written by Paul McCartney, who said the image of Mother Mary came from a dream about his own mother, Mary.

question.text: What figure does the giant statue overlooking Rio de Janeiro depict?

results.hint: Its open arms echo a central figure in Christian iconography.
results.explanation: Jesus Christ is depicted by the statue known as Christ the Redeemer, which stands atop Corcovado Mountain.

question.text: Which American music duo released the song 'Mrs. Robinson'?

results.hint: The pair also recorded “The Sound of Silence” and “Bridge over Troubled Water.”
results.explanation: Simon & Garfunkel's recording appeared in The Graduate; Paul Simon wrote the song.

question.text: With which sport is Babe Ruth associated?

results.hint: His legendary home runs came while playing for the New York Yankees.
results.explanation: Babe Ruth's home-run hitting helped make the New York Yankees a dominant team in the 1920s. He remains one of baseball's most famous players.

question.text: In which country is the city of Shenzhen?

results.hint: Shenzhen sits in Guangdong, just across the border from Hong Kong.
results.explanation: Shenzhen grew into a major technology and manufacturing hub after becoming one of China's first special economic zones.

question.text: Which expert should you call if you're building with stone?

results.hint: This building tradesperson lays bricks and sets them with mortar.
results.explanation: A mason works with stone and brick, often building or repairing walls, chimneys, and foundations.

question.text: In what movie does the main character have a friend called Bubba Blue who dreams of opening up his own shrimping business?

results.hint: Its title character famously runs across the country and encounters several moments in American history.
results.explanation: Forrest Gump fulfills Bubba’s dream by becoming a shrimp boat captain, and the success makes him wealthy.

question.text: How long does a human pregnancy last?

results.hint: Doctors divide the usual gestation into three trimesters of roughly equal length.
results.explanation: A typical pregnancy lasts about 40 weeks when counted from the first day of the last menstrual period, though birth timing varies.

question.text: In football (soccer), which player uses their hands stop the opposition scoring?

results.hint: They guard the net and are usually the only teammate allowed to handle the ball in their own penalty area.
results.explanation: A goalkeeper may handle the ball only inside their own penalty area; outside it, the same handling rules apply as for teammates.
